content.content:
416	#### Step 4.4 — `ZimmCartItemActions` + pending-item-across-auth
417	
418	**Changes.** Remove / Move to Wishlist as **underlined text links below the stepper** (SFCC-270 AC8, styled in B3's pass). Gap **24px**, not Figma's raw 25px — §11.10(4), snapped to the nearest tokenised value with a comment saying the design specified 25. Links `capitalize`, `textStyle="linkSm"`, `link/default` → `--zimm-color-text-default`.
419	
420	Note the actions are **not** inside base `product-item` — it receives them as a `secondaryActions` prop from its caller. So this molecule is supplied by the container, and we do not fight the base structure to inject it.
421	
422	Remove: item removed, drawer count decrements, totals update; quantity > 1 removes all units in one action.
423	
424	Wishlist, guest: the existing `ZimmWishlistAuthDrawer` via `useWishlistAuthDrawer`, **one hook instance**, `intentId: 'cart-wishlist'`. Per gate #5, this is a **deliberate override** of two sources that say "login page" (SFCC-272 AC7 and Confluence CAI-018), justified by consistency with the four other auth-drawer surfaces — record it as an override, not as an AC reading. The `.docs/prd/cart.md` §2 paraphrase is the weaker justification and should not be the one cited.
425	
426	**Clarified 2026-09-20, found by this step's own Implementer:** "one hook instance" does **not** mean `ZimmCartItemActions` calls `useWishlistAuthDrawer` itself — that component renders once per cart line (it's `product-item`'s own `secondaryActions` prop, and `product-item` renders once per line), so a direct call would mount N instances in an N-item cart, exactly the cardinality this same step's own "Rejected and not to be revisited" paragraph below already forbids. The one real instance lives **hoisted above every row**, in step 4.6's `cartDrawerContainer.tsx` — `ZimmCartItemActions` instead receives `isGuest: boolean` and `onGuestWishlistClick: () => void` as props (the same callback-prop shape `onRemove`/`onMoveToWishlist` already use), and step 4.6 is responsible for actually wiring the one real `useWishlistAuthDrawer`/`ZimmWishlistAuthDrawer` pair and threading these two props into every row.
427	
428	Pending item held in **React state** (covers email-code and create-account, where the page never unloads) **and** session storage (covers the Apple/Google redirect). Read state first, fall back to storage, clear **both** together. Same **5-minute** age bound as the hook's own intent (`PENDING_WISHLIST_INTENT_MAX_AGE_MS`), so a stale item cannot be resumed.
429	
430	Rejected and not to be revisited: one hook instance per line item (mounts a `useForm`, three `useAuthHelper`s, a `useAuthModal` and a drawer **per row** — a ten-item bag mounts ten of each, against a stated mobile-page-speed priority); adding an optional `itemId` to the shared `PendingWishlistIntent` (better long-term, but changes a shared hook with three existing call sites — raise separately).
431	
432	**Pass criteria — both links are interactive controls, so every state is named:**
433	1. Default: underlined, capitalized, `--zimm-color-text-default`, 24px gap, height 24 / py 4.
434	2. **Hover, focus-visible** inherited from `ZimmLink`'s recipe. Assert the focus-visible ring is **not identical** to default. Figma supplies only the `link/default` token for these links; inheritance is the resolution, annotated. If `ZimmLink` turns out to carry no focus treatment, that is an open question at that moment — not something to leave for the Tester. **Corrected 2026-09-20** — this criterion previously also listed "active." Checked against `ZimmLink`'s real recipe (`zimmLink.css.ts`) during this step's own build: `ZimmLink` genuinely has no `_active` state anywhere, hover and focus-visible are the only two real ones. Don't fabricate an active-state assertion to satisfy a criterion that overclaimed what the inherited atom actually has.
435	3. Disabled: **not specified in Figma for these links and not required by any AC.** Do not build one.
436	4. Remove with quantity 1 → one `removeItemFromBasket` call, count decrements by 1.
437	5. Remove with quantity 3 → **one** call, count decrements by 3 (AC3 — all units in one action, not three calls).
438	6. Authenticated wishlist move, quantity 3 → all units removed from cart, **a single SKU saved** to wishlist, count decrements by 3, product-named success message emitted (AC5). **This criterion also closes step 4.3's own deferred pass criterion 3** (added 2026-09-20): this is the first step that actually renders something a shopper can trigger one of `useCartMessages`'s three messages from, so this is where the Storybook `play`/`within(document.body)`/portal-exception proof that `useCartMessages.ts` itself couldn't provide finally lands — assert it here, on the real triggering interaction, not as a separate synthetic story.
439

562	
563	Six real, currently-shipped defects were found in commits already scored PASS on Design fidelity,
564	by a from-scratch re-audit that rendered the real components live instead of reading source and
565	Figma side by side. Every one of the six traces back to one of the gaps below. These are now
566	mandatory for every remaining step's Design-fidelity check — not optional rigor, a gate. When
567	dispatching Tester/Scorer for 3.6 onward, brief them with this section explicitly: they start
568	each run with no memory of today, so the standard has to be restated, not assumed carried over.
569	
570	1. **A rendered-output claim needs a live measurement citation, not a source read.** "The recipe
571	   sets `fontWeight: 500`" is not the same claim as "the rendered text measures `font-weight: 500`
572	   in a real browser" — the first can be true while the second is false. Every Design-fidelity
573	   PASS from here on cites an actual measured value (computed style, bounding box, or a real
574	   screenshot) against the actual Figma-sourced value, for every property being signed off, not
575	   just the ones that seem most at-risk.
576	2. **A wrapper's correct style does not prove a nested element inherits it.** Two of the six
577	   defects were exactly this shape: `textStyle`/`fontWeight` correctly set on a container, silently
578	   lost before reaching the actual visible text, because the nested element was either a Chakra
579	   component with its own competing theme registration (`Heading`, and by extension `Button`/
580	   `IconButton`/`Modal`/anything imported from `@chakra-ui/react` un-wrapped in a plain `chakra.*`
581	   factory) or a literal HTML tag with its own default rendering (`<b>`, via a base SFCC
582	   component). Whenever a style is applied above a boundary like that, verify the leaf text node's
583	   own computed style directly — inheritance is not something to assume across it.
584	3. **A previously-recorded "confirmed correct" is not permanent proof.** This exact document's own
585	   audit trail (`figma-reference/discrepancies.md`) both found real bugs *and*, twice, had to
586	   retract its own "confirmed" claims once they were checked against a real render instead of
587	   restated from a prior pass. Re-verify against a live render before citing an earlier pass as
588	   settled, especially for anything touching the same file again.
589	4. **Storybook `play` functions auto-run on load.** A live check against a story with a `play`
590	   function is measuring the *post-play* state by the time any normal wait resolves, not the
591	   initial seed — sample within ~100ms of mount if the true initial state matters, and never treat
592	   a play function's own scripted end-state as a seeding bug.
593	5. **Read the real, current JSX before asserting how two elements relate.** More than one
594	   mis-scoped finding this pass came from reasoning about layout from a written description
595	   instead of the actual current source — siblings vs. nested, same container vs. different, is
596	   checkable in seconds and shouldn't be inferred.
597	6. **A fix for one interaction can silently break a different one.** The focus-ring fix's first
598	   attempt passed its own new test and broke backdrop-click-to-close, undetected until the full
599	   existing suite was re-run. Any interaction/focus/event-handling change re-runs the component's
600	   *entire* existing test suite, not just the new assertion, before being called done.
601	7. **Mutation-test every new test, and disclose when jsdom genuinely can't.** Revert the fix,
602	   confirm the new test fails with the real wrong value; restore, confirm it passes. If a property
603	   (native `:focus-visible` matching is the known example so far) can't be made mutation-sensitive
604	   under jsdom, say so directly in the test's own comment rather than claim proof the test doesn't
605	   actually provide — the real proof in that case is the live-browser verification, cited as such.
606	8. **No AI attribution, no third-person references to any person, in any commit message.**
607	   Objective and technical only — what changed and why, not who caught it or confirmed it. Two
608	   rounds of whole-branch correction this pass were both this exact category.
609	9. **A green Vitest suite does not prove a `.stories.tsx` file actually renders (added 2026-09-20,
610	   after step 4.4 shipped four crashing stories through an entire round-0 build, its Tester's Full
611	   loop, and its own Orchestrator, all green).** `ZimmCartItemActions` called `ZimmLink`, which
612	   calls `useSafeHref()` unconditionally, which needs a `MultiSiteProvider` the story never
613	   supplied — every sibling component that already uses `ZimmLink` (`footer`, `zimmSizeSelector`,
614	   `zimmNavItem`, `zimmSearchInput`, `zimmLink`'s own story) already carries the decorator this one
615	   was missing. `index.test.tsx`'s own Vitest suite mocked `useSafeHref` away specifically to avoid
616	   this exact hazard — correctly, for a unit test — which is precisely why it could never have
617	   caught a *Storybook*-level failure of the same hazard; the two layers were never actually
618	   testing the same thing. **Any step that creates or meaningfully changes a `.stories.tsx` file
619	   must actually build and serve Storybook and run `test-storybook --ci` (or equivalent — open each
620	   changed story in a real browser and confirm no error boundary) before that step can be scored,
621	   not just read the `play` function and assume it executes.** This is a different failure mode
622	   than points 1–7 above (which are about a story rendering the *wrong* thing) — this is about
623	   whether it renders *at all*, and no other gate in this loop checks for it.
624	
625	## 6. Open questions
626	
627	These block the handoff. None is a decision I should make for you.
628	
629	1. **`.github/workflows/qa.yml` is Tier 1 and owner approval is not confirmed.** B0 is BLOCKED until either the authenticated `gh` login is verified in `@ZimmermannAU/tier-1-approvers` or a named approving review is secured. import { defineStyleConfig } from '@chakra-ui/react';

/**
 * Recipe — the "Remove" / "Move to Wishlist" action-links row (SFCC-270 AC8, SFCC-272). Single
 * style, no parts: both links get their full visual treatment from `ZimmLink`'s own recipe
 * (`zimmLink.css.ts`, size `small` — capitalize, 12px/500/14px-lh, plus that recipe's own
 * hover/focus-visible states); this recipe only owns the row's own layout, matching
 * `zimmLink/zimmLink.css.ts`'s own single-style shape rather than
 * `zimmQuantityStepper.css.ts`'s multi-part one, since there is no second visual sub-part here to
 * name.
 *
 * `gap` — Figma specifies 25px (§11.10(4) of the SFCC-11 plan); no `--zimm-scale-*` step lands on
 * 25 (foundation/spacing.ts's steps go ...m:16px, l:20px, xl:24px, 2xl:32px... — confirmed no
 * 25px entry), so this snaps to the nearest existing token, 24px (`xl`), and records the raw
 * design value here rather than typing an unregistered one-off literal.
 *
 * `color` on each link is NOT set here: `ZimmLink`'s own `link.default` alias
 * (`foundation/colour.ts:87`, `grey[900]`) and `foundation/colour.ts:61`'s `text.default` (also
 * `grey[900]`) are the same primitive, so plain `<ZimmLink>` already renders the colour this
 * component's own spec calls for — adding a second, competing colour declaration here would be
 * exactly the anti-pattern `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md`'s "One canonical styling surface
 * per component type" section warns against (a value that can drift from the atom's own recipe
 * over time instead of there being only one place it's declared).
 */
export const ZimmCartItemActions = defineStyleConfig({
  baseStyle: {
    display: 'flex',
    alignItems: 'center',
    gap: 'var(--zimm-scale-xl)', // Figma: 25px, snapped to the nearest token (24px)
  },
});

1	import { useEffect, useState } from 'react';
2	import {
3	  clearSessionJSONItem,
4	  getSessionJSONItem,
5	  setSessionJSONItem,
6	} from '@salesforce/retail-react-app/app/utils/utils';
7	
8	/**
9	 * Outcome of one wishlist-move attempt. The actual SFCC SDK calls (wishlist add + cart removal)
10	 * are the caller's own responsibility — SFCC-11 plan step 4.6 (`cartDrawerContainer.tsx`, not
11	 * built yet) — this file only reports what happened, matching the exact discriminated-union
12	 * pattern `useCartMergeAndCap.ts`'s own `CartCapResult` already established
13	 * (`overrides/app/hooks/useCartMergeAndCap.ts:25-29`), per typescript.md's stated preference for
14	 * a discriminated union over a pile of optional fields.
15	 */
16	export type WishlistMoveResult =
17	  | { status: 'success' }
18	  | { status: 'already-in-wishlist' }
19	  | { status: 'error'; error: unknown };
20	
21	/**
22	 * sessionStorage key PREFIX for "a guest asked to move THIS specific cart line to their wishlist
23	 * before authenticating." Namespaced per `productId` — see `pendingWishlistCartItemKey` below —
24	 * so that two different cart rows' pending intents can never collide in a single shared slot: a
25	 * guest beginning a pending move on row A, then row B, before either completes a redirect-based
26	 * auth flow, must leave both independently resumable rather than row B's write silently
27	 * overwriting row A's. Deliberately a distinct mechanism, and a distinct key, from
28	 * `useWishlistAuthDrawer.ts`'s own `PENDING_WISHLIST_INTENT_KEY`
29	 * (`overrides/app/hooks/useWishlistAuthDrawer.ts:43`): that key answers "which mounted drawer
30	 * instance's `onAuthSuccess` should fire after a social-IDP redirect" — its own
31	 * `PendingWishlistIntent` type carries only `intentId`/`timestamp`, no item identity at all.
32	 * This hook answers a different question — "which cart LINE was pending" — so it is a new,
33	 * separate mechanism rather than an addition to that shared type. The SFCC-11 plan explicitly
34	 * rejects adding an `itemId` field to that shared type: it has three other existing call sites
35	 * (header/rightBar, drawer-menu, product-view) and changing it is out of this step's scope.
36	 */
37	const PENDING_WISHLIST_CART_ITEM_KEY_PREFIX = 'zimmPendingWishlistCartItem';
38	
39	/**
40	 * Builds the per-product sessionStorage key — see `PENDING_WISHLIST_CART_ITEM_KEY_PREFIX`'s own
41	 * doc for why storage is namespaced this way instead of one shared key.
42	 */
43	const pendingWishlistCartItemKey = (productId: string): string =>
44	  `${PENDING_WISHLIST_CART_ITEM_KEY_PREFIX}:${productId}`;
45	
46	/**
47	 * Same 5-minute bound as `useWishlistAuthDrawer.ts`'s own `PENDING_WISHLIST_INTENT_MAX_AGE_MS`
48	 * (`overrides/app/hooks/useWishlistAuthDrawer.ts:52` — `5 * 60 * 1000`), and the same reasoning:
49	 * long enough for a real auth round trip, short enough that a long-abandoned attempt cannot
50	 * misfire later against a much later, unrelated cart session. Not imported from that file — the
51	 * constant is not exported there, and this step does not modify that file (out of scope; see the
52	 * SFCC-11 plan step 4.4's manifest and its "explicitly rejected" list). Redefined here as an
53	 * independent, same-valued constant instead.
54	 */
55	const PENDING_WISHLIST_MAX_AGE_MS = 5 * 60 * 1000; // 5 minutes
56	
57	type PendingWishlistCartItem = {
58	  /**
59	   * Matched against this row's own `productId`, not `itemId` — deliberate. A guest's basket may
60	   * be merged into a registered customer's basket between the guest's click and the shopper
61	   * completing auth (SFCC-250 step 4.1, `useWishlistAuthDrawer.ts`'s own `isRegistered` effect),
62	   * and that merge can change which `itemId` a given product line carries (it merges into a
63	   * destination basket via `createDestinationBasket: true`). `productId` is stable across that
64	   * boundary; `itemId` is not — keying the match on `itemId` would risk silently failing to
65	   * resume a legitimate pending move the moment a merge has actually happened. See this step's
66	   * own report for the related, still-open sequencing question this raises for step 4.6.
67	   */
68	  productId: string;
69	  timestamp: number;
70	};
71	
72	export type UsePendingWishlistItemParams = {
73	  /** Identifies this cart line for matching a resumed intent — see PendingWishlistCartItem's own
74	   *  doc comment for why this is `productId`, not `itemId`. */
75	  productId: string;
76	  /** Whether the current shopper is unauthenticated. Passed down from the caller (e.g. read once
77	   *  from `useCustomerType()` at the cart container) rather than read by this hook itself — see
78	   *  `zimmCartItemActions/index.tsx`'s own architecture note for why. */
79	  isGuest: boolean;
80	  /** Called (no arguments) once a previously-pending move for THIS row should be attempted.
81	   *  Fires at most once per stored intent — never for another row's pending item, never twice
82	   *  for the same one. */
83	  onResume: () => void | Promise<void>;
84	};
85	
86	export type UsePendingWishlistItemReturn = {
87	  /** Call when a guest clicks "Move to Wishlist" for this row — persists the pending intent to
88	   *  both React state (survives the email-code/create-account flows, which never unload the
89	   *  page) and session storage (survives the Apple/Google redirect, which reloads it), so
90	   *  `onResume` fires automatically once `isGuest` becomes false for this same product. */
91	  beginPendingMove: () => void;
92	};
93	
94	/**
95	 * Hook — persists a guest's "move to wishlist" intent for one cart line across an authentication
96	 * step, and resumes it once the shopper is no longer a guest. Extracted per
97	 * `.claude/rules/components.md`'s extract-to-hook threshold: this is React state plus a
98	 * non-trivial effect (session-storage read/write/clear, a 5-minute age check, resuming after a
99	 * simulated page reload) that would otherwise sit inline in `ZimmCartItemActions`.
100	 *
101	 * Deliberately calls no auth or `commerce-sdk-react` hook itself — `isGuest` arrives as a plain
102	 * prop, and the actual move (`onResume`) is the caller's own already-composed function. Only ONE
103	 * `useWishlistAuthDrawer` instance may exist for the whole cart (SFCC-11 plan step 4.4's own
104	 * explicit rejection of "one per line item"), so that real hook cannot live inside a component
105	 * that mounts once per cart line — this hook stays calling-hook-free so it can safely mount once
106	 * per row, alongside it, without reproducing that rejected shape.
107	 *
108	 * @returns `beginPendingMove`, the one function a guest click calls.
109	 */
110	export const usePendingWishlistItem = ({
111	  productId,
112	  isGuest,
113	  onResume,
114	}: UsePendingWishlistItemParams): UsePendingWishlistItemReturn => {
115	  const [pending, setPending] = useState<PendingWishlistCartItem | undefined>(undefined);
116	
117	  const beginPendingMove = () => {
118	    const intent: PendingWishlistCartItem = { productId, timestamp: Date.now() };
119	    setPending(intent);
120	    setSessionJSONItem(pendingWishlistCartItemKey(productId), intent);
121	  };
122	
123	  // Mirrors useWishlistAuthDrawer.ts's own redirect-consuming effect (that file's second
124	  // useEffect, [isRegistered]-only deps, overrides/app/hooks/useWishlistAuthDrawer.ts:252-259) —
125	  // runs on mount and on every `isGuest` change, not only on a true-to-false transition, because
126	  // a fresh mount after a real page reload (Apple/Google redirect) already has `isGuest === false`
127	  // on its very first render, with no transition to observe.
128	  useEffect(() => {
129	    if (isGuest) return;
130	
131	    const stored = getSessionJSONItem(pendingWishlistCartItemKey(productId)) as PendingWishlistCartItem | undefined;
132	    // The per-product key above already means `stored` can only ever be what THIS row itself
133	    // wrote — a different row's pending intent lives under its own, different key and is never
134	    // read, resumed, or cleared from here. This productId match is a defensive belt-and-suspenders
135	    // check on top of that (never act on foreign/malformed data even if it somehow ended up in
136	    // this slot), not the mechanism that keeps two rows apart.
137	    const mineFromStorage = stored?.productId === productId ? stored : undefined;
138	    const candidate = pending ?? mineFromStorage;
139	    if (!candidate) return;
140	
141	    // Found something of mine — clear both stores now, regardless of whether it turns out to be
142	    // fresh or stale below (a stale intent must not linger either — nothing resumes it later).
143	    // Only ever clears THIS row's own key — another row's still-pending intent, under its own
144	    // key, is untouched.
145	    setPending(undefined);
146	    clearSessionJSONItem(pendingWishlistCartItemKey(productId));
147	
148	    const isFresh = Date.now() - candidate.timestamp <= PENDING_WISHLIST_MAX_AGE_MS;
149	    if (isFresh) {
150	      void onResume();
151	    }
152	  }, [isGuest]);
153	
154	  return { beginPendingMove };
155	};

## Bottom line

**PASS.** The round-2 Storybook fix is real — I rebuilt Storybook from scratch myself, served it on an isolated port, and ran real headless-Chromium tests against it. All four stories render and pass, with zero console errors. The step is safe to commit. One small, pre-existing gap surfaced during the deepest Design-fidelity check I ran (a 2px link-height shortfall) — it's real, but it lives in a shared atom outside this step's file set, so I'm flagging it rather than gating on it. Details below.

This is round 3 of the score, not round 3 of REWORK — round 2's fix passed, so nothing here needs to escalate.

## Per-axis table (most severe finding first)

| Axis | Verdict | Evidence |
|---|---|---|
| **Design fidelity** | PASS, with one disclosed non-blocking gap | Rebuilt Storybook fresh (`npm run build-storybook` into an isolated scratch dir, not reusing any prior build), served it on port 6007 (separate from the ambient dev server already running on 6006 — confirmed pre-existing, untouched), ran `test-storybook --ci --verbose --failOnConsole` against it: **4/4 stories pass, zero console errors.** Went further with live Playwright measurements against the real rendered DOM (not source reads): row `gap: 24px` (matches `var(--zimm-scale-xl)` = 1.5rem), link `font-size: 12px` / `font-weight: 500` / `line-height: 14px` / `text-transform: capitalize` / `text-decoration: underline`, `color: rgb(25,25,25)` (= `#191919` = `grey[900]`, confirmed the *identical* primitive backs both `text.default` and `link.default` in `colour.ts`, not just a visually-close value). Live keyboard-Tab confirmed focus-visible genuinely differs from default (`outline: none` → `outline: solid 1px`). Live mouse-hover confirmed hover genuinely differs (`rgb(25,25,25)` → `rgb(98,98,98)`). Toast copy confirmed verbatim against `useCartMessages.ts`'s actual ICU strings. **One real finding:** the plan's own pass criterion 1 states "height 24" for the link; live-measured rendered height is 22px (4px padding + 4px padding + 14px line-height). Root cause is entirely in `zimmLink.css.ts`'s `sm` size (`overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmLink/zimmLink.css.ts:44-48`) — a file step 4.4 doesn't touch, doesn't own, and reuses correctly per this codebase's own "one canonical styling surface" rule. Fixing it here would mean editing a shared atom consumed by footer/zimmSizeSelector/zimmNavItem/zimmSearchInput too — out of this step's manifest, not a round-3 fix. See defect entry below. |
| **Correctness** | PASS | `npx tsc --noEmit`: exit 0, zero output (ran fresh, myself). Scoped `npx vitest run` on the component folder: 21/21 tests green (`index.test.tsx` 10, `usePendingWishlistItem.test.ts` 11). `recipeGuards.test.ts`: 6/6 green (bare-token-key + namespacing guards). Did not re-run the full 1673-test suite myself — `vitest.config.ts` only includes `*.test.ts(x)`, so a `.stories.tsx`-only diff structurally cannot affect it, and it was already run fresh immediately after this exact diff per the report. No outstanding 🔴 findings. |
| **Pass criteria** | PASS | Criteria 1–3, 6–9 evidenced directly (unit tests + story plays + my own live measurements); 4/5 correctly proven only on the callback-firing half (component never receives `quantity`, count/SKU half is step 4.6's to prove — already correctly disclosed, not a gap in this step); criterion 10 covered exhaustively in `usePendingWishlistItem.test.ts`; criterion 11 correctly deferred to step 4.2's already-passed order test. The one shortfall (criterion 1's "height 24") is the Design-fidelity finding above, not a criteria-tracking failure. |
| **Completeness** | PASS | Story present, 4 named exports for meaningful states (not a combinatorial dump). Test present for both the component and the extracted hook. Test describe-block titles map 1:1 to the plan's own pass-criterion numbers — unusually good traceability, verified by reading the file, not assumed. |
| **Conformance** | PASS | `zimmCartItemActions.css.ts` uses only `var(--zimm-scale-xl)`, no bare token keys, declares no competing colour/hover/focus (correctly leaves those to `ZimmLink`'s own recipe). `theme/components/index.ts` registration is a minimal, correctly-placed one-line-plus-import addition. `ZimmLink` is imported via the `app/` alias, not the SFCC base path — correct per overrideStyling.md's "importing an already-overridden component" rule. Story decorator is a byte-for-byte match of `zimmLink/index.stories.tsx`'s own current decorator, as claimed. |
| **Restraint** | PASS | `git status` shows exactly two touched paths repo-wide: the new `zimmCartItemActions/` folder and the one-line `theme/components/index.ts` registration — nothing outside the Orchestrator's already-confirmed scope. File mtimes are consistent with round 2 touching only `index.stories.tsx` (latest by ~26 minutes). On my own side: I did not re-run the full Vitest suite or redo round-1's mutation testing (unchanged files, already confirmed); the additional live-browser checks I added were scoped specifically to closing the one criterion (#2, focus-visible) that had never received live-browser evidence in any prior round — proportionate to the explicit "scrutinize Design fidelity hardest" brief, not padding. |

## Overall: PASS

## What I tried to falsify

- **That the round-2 fix actually works, not just that the Implementer said so.** Rebuilt Storybook from a clean scratch directory (not the Implementer's build, not the ambient dev server), served it in isolation, ran `test-storybook` with `--failOnConsole` added (stricter than what was claimed) against real headless Chromium. It passed clean. This is the load-bearing check this round exists for, and I did not accept the claim on faith.
- **That the ambient port-6006 process wasn't secretly propping up the result.** Confirmed it's a separate, pre-existing process (started 4:12pm, well before this check), and ran everything against my own isolated port 6007 instead, so the result can't be attributed to stale/cached state on 6006.
- **That "gap 24px" and the ZimmLink states are real, not just correctly typed.** Per verification-standard point 1, a recipe read is not proof of rendered output — I took live `getComputedStyle`/`getBoundingClientRect` measurements via Playwright against the actual rendered story, including real keyboard-Tab and mouse-hover interactions, not just reading the `_focusVisible`/`_hover` objects in source. This is where the one real finding (22px vs 24px) surfaced — a source read alone would have missed it, since the source values (padding 4px, line-height 14px) are each individually correct in isolation and only reveal the shortfall when summed against a live box.
- **That "colour matches" wasn't just "close enough."** Traced `text.default` and `link.default` back to `colour.ts` and confirmed they resolve to the literal same primitive (`grey[900]` = `#191919`), then confirmed the live-rendered `rgb(25,25,25)` matches exactly — not approximately.
- **That the Orchestrator's "no new scope" call holds.** Checked `git status` myself rather than relying on the round-2 report's own description of what it touched.

## What I could not verify

- **The full, final visual checkpoint against Figma is still Marcel's/a designer's to do — see below.** My live measurements confirm *token-level* correctness (the right CSS values are actually reaching the DOM), which is a different and narrower claim than "a human confirms this looks right against the Figma frame." That axis is UNVERIFIED in the human-eyeball sense until that checkpoint happens, even though I'm scoring Design fidelity PASS on everything mechanically checkable.
- **How this looks inside a real cart line.** `ZimmCartItemActions` only renders standalone in Storybook right now — `cartDrawerContainer.tsx` (step 4.6) doesn't exist yet, so "does this sit correctly below the real quantity stepper, in the real drawer, at real widths" cannot be checked yet by anyone, not just by me. That's expected at this point in the build, not a gap in this step.
- **I did not re-run the full 1673-test Vitest suite or the a11y Storybook addon.** Deliberate, not an oversight — see the Restraint row above for why.

## Defect found (disclosed, non-blocking for this step)

**`overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmLink/zimmLink.css.ts:44-48`** (the `sm` size) — CONFIRMED via live measurement: rendered link height is 22px (4px + 4px padding-block + 14px line-height), 2px short of the 24px this step's own pass criterion 1 and the recipe's own WCAG 2.5.8 comment both target. Not a defect of step 4.4's own diff — `zimmCartItemActions` correctly reuses this atom rather than adding a competing height declaration (exactly what this codebase's "one canonical styling surface" rule asks for). Fixing it means changing `sm`'s line-height token for a shared atom with 4+ other consumers (footer, zimmSizeSelector, zimmNavItem, zimmSearchInput) — outside step 4.4's manifest. **Instruction: do not fix inside step 4.4.** Log it in `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md`'s "Known gaps" section next to the existing `zimmButton.css.ts` height-mismatch entry (same shape of issue, same project precedent for how it's tracked), and raise the actual fix as its own small, separately-scoped step so its blast radius across the other four consumers gets checked deliberately rather than as a side effect of a cart-step REWORK.

## Marcel visual checkpoint — still owed, and now actually usable

Yes, still owed — my checks prove the tokens are reaching the DOM correctly, not that a human has looked at it next to Figma. But the checklist from last pass is now genuinely usable, because the crash that made it impossible is fixed. Updated checklist:

- **URLs** (ambient dev server, already running on 6006): `http://localhost:6006/?path=/story/commerce-zimmcartitemactions--default`, `--wishlistmovesuccess`, `--alreadyinwishlist`, `--guestclick`.
- **Correct looks like:** two underlined text links reading "Remove" then "Move to Wishlist" (capitalized per-word, not shouty all-caps), sitting close together (~24px gap), near-black at rest, visibly lighter grey on hover, a visible outline ring when Tabbed to (there's none at rest).
- **Incorrect looks like:** links rendered as boxed/bordered buttons (wrong component substituted), ALL-CAPS text (means the small/large size branch is swapped), no visible change on hover or Tab, or the toast copy on `WishlistMoveSuccess` not reading exactly "Cloud 91 Small Clutch added to Wishlist".
- **New item to ask about specifically:** whether the ~22px vs 24px link height (flagged above) needs a real fix or is fine as shipped — that's a call for whoever owns `zimmLink.css.ts`, not this step.
- **Caveat, unchanged from before:** this can only be checked in isolation right now, not inside a real cart line — step 4.6 doesn't exist yet.

## What Marcel is missing

Nothing new this pass beyond what's already flagged above (the `zimmLink.css.ts` height gap) — but worth naming plainly since it's easy to miss: that gap is going to recur on every future step that reuses `ZimmLink` at `size="small"` (there are already 4 other consumers, and this step makes it 5) until someone deliberately fixes the shared atom. Each new consumer will keep inheriting the same 2px shortfall silently, because no single step "owns" fixing a shared dependency it merely consumes correctly. Worth a standalone small ticket rather than waiting for a sixth component to notice it independently.

It passed clean. This is the load-bearing check this round exists for, and I did not accept the claim on faith.

- **That "gap 24px" and the ZimmLink states are real, not just correctly typed.** Per verification-standard point 1, a recipe read is not proof of rendered output — I took live `getComputedStyle`/`getBoundingClientRect` measurements via Playwright against the actual rendered story, including real keyboard-Tab and mouse-hover interactions, not just reading the `_focusVisible`/`_hover` objects in source. This is where the one real finding (22px vs 24px) surfaced — a source read alone would have missed it, since the source values (padding 4px, line-height 14px) are each individually correct in isolation and only reveal the shortfall when summed against a live box.
- **That "colour matches" wasn't just "close enough."** Traced `text.default` and `link.default` back to `colour.ts` and confirmed they resolve to the literal same primitive (`grey[900]` = `#191919`), then confirmed the live-rendered `rgb(25,25,25)` matches exactly — not approximately.

## Defect found (disclosed, non-blocking for this step)

**`overrides/app/components/ui-kits/atoms/zimmLink/zimmLink.css.ts:44-48`** (the `sm` size) — CONFIRMED via live measurement: rendered link height is 22px (4px + 4px padding-block + 14px line-height), 2px short of the 24px this step's own pass criterion 1 and the recipe's own WCAG 2.5.8 comment both target. Not a defect of step 4.4's own diff — `zimmCartItemActions` correctly reuses this atom rather than adding a competing height declaration (exactly what this codebase's "one canonical styling surface" rule asks for). Fixing it means changing `sm`'s line-height token for a shared atom with 4+ other consumers (footer, zimmSizeSelector, zimmNavItem, zimmSearchInput) — outside step 4.4's manifest. **Instruction: do not fix inside step 4.4.** Log it in `.claude/rules/overrideStyling.md`'s "Known gaps" section next to the existing `zimmButton.css.ts` height-mismatch entry (same shape of issue, same project precedent for how it's tracked), and raise the actual fix as its own small, separately-scoped step so its blast radius across the other four consumers gets checked deliberately rather than as a side effect of a cart-step REWORK.

Nothing new this pass beyond what's already flagged above (the `zimmLink.css.ts` height gap) — but worth naming plainly since it's easy to miss: that gap is going to recur on every future step that reuses `ZimmLink` at `size="small"` (there are already 4 other consumers, and this step makes it 5) until someone deliberately fixes the shared atom.
